# Master AI with Google Antigravity: From Coding to Orchestration of Agents

A summary of Google's live feed on Antigravity news. Video shows how to work with AI agents without losing control of code: projects in Agent Manager 2.0, approval before changing files, short chats with /learn, sandboxes with Git worktree and subagents.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on July 17, 2026 (8 min 40 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LVEj-aRVVKE

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The problem: an agent breaking stable code

For those who program with AI, the biggest concern is an agent changing, without supervision, a code base that was stable [00:00]. The video summarizes Google's latest live feed on Antigravity and transforms new features into everyday practices [00:21].

Rod, of Google's Developer Relations team, says that in AI there is not a single way to do something, and that this makes room to reduce repetitive work [00:41]. The idea is to release time for engineering and design [01:02].

## What changed in Antigravity

- At Agent Manager 2.0, former workspaces have turned **projects**. A project brings together several repositories linked together, such as frontend, backend and documentation [01:45].
- When a database table changes, the AI generates a report with the impact of change on the entire project [02:07].
- CLI has gained a mode of approval with Shift+Tab: the agent plans what he will do and waits for human review before changing any file [02:29].
- CLI also gained scheduled tasks in the background, the /search command in the source code and a thinner permission control [02:51].

## context limits: short chats and /learn command

The broadcast recommends a four-step cycle: open a new chat, solve a single task, run the /learn command and archive the conversation [03:12]. A very long chat spends tokens and leaves AI lost [03:35].

The /learn bridge between one chat and the next. Before filing the conversation, it extracts the rules and patterns and records everything in a permanent context Markdown file of the project [03:58].

## Sandboxes with Git worktree

Git worktree is a resource of Git himself. It checks out several branches of the same repository in separate folders, which share the same history [04:18].

In the ancient flow, a refactoring that breaks in the middle leaves the project in a difficult state to reverse [04:40]. With the worktree, the AI tests in an isolated folder. If it works, you do the merge. If it goes wrong, delete the folder, and the main branch remains intact [05:03].

## Defensive programming with AI

AI accelerates work, but can also bring vulnerabilities if there is no supervision [05:23]. The rule is to program as if everyone who calls the application had bad intentions, and to ask the AI, in the prompt itself, to treat extreme cases of security [05:44].

- Block access to files outside the root directory [05:44].
- Never commit API keys [05:44].
- Ask agents to keep packages and dependencies up to date, to avoid known failures [06:04].

## MCP and subagents

MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects the agent to external tools such as a remote database or Figma [06:04]. The team warns: activate these tools with selection, project by project, because the MCP consumes the agent's context memory [06:25].

Subagents are minor agents, created by an orchestrating agent for limited scope tasks. One takes care of the frontend, another of the connection with the database, and a third testes what the two wrote [06:46].

According to the video, the Antigravity orchestra subagents at up to 10 levels of depth: one subagent can call another, which calls another [07:07].

The /btw ("by the way") command serves for quick orders such as generating the colors of a new theme without polluting the main chat [07:28].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How to prevent the agent from changing files without revision?

In CLI, use Shift+Tab approval mode: the agent shows the plan and waits for revision before changing files [02:29].

### What's the command /learn for?

To save what the conversation solved in a project context Markdown file before archiving the chat [03:58].

## About the video

Welcome to the future of software development! In this video, we dive into the latest updates of Google Antigravity, exploring how the tool is reducing manual work and transforming developers into true intelligent system orchestrators
.
Follow Rodie, the leader of Developer Relations, on a detailed technical journey on how to use AI effectively to scale your projects, from small applications to large systems
.
What you will learn in this video:
CLI vs. Agent Manager 2.0: Understand the strategic differences between the command line interface (CLI) and the 2.0 agent manager (the command center for multiple projects)
.
Security with Git Work Trees: Learn to use native work tree support as safe sandboxes to experience drastic changes without losing progress or breaking your main branch
.
Sub-agent Orchestration: Find out how to create agent hierarchies up to 10 depth levels, allowing an AI to coordinate specific backend, frontend and code revision tasks simultaneously
.
Context optimization with /learn: See how the new /learn command helps transform conversations into knowledge artifacts and new skills for your agents, saving tokens and improving accuracy
.
Sidecar automation: Learn how to set up scheduled maintenance tasks such as memory health checks and automatic backups, allowing agents to work for themselves when you are offline
.
Programming Defensive with AI: Improve the security of your applications by requesting extreme case reviews and malicious attacks directly on your agents from the first day of development
.
